domain_1:
    action in domain_1: (:action princess_accepts_with_heart :parameters (?k ?p - entity) :precondition (and (rema_np__p_married ?p ?k) (not (with_all_my_heart_spoken))) :effect (with_all_my_heart_spoken))
    predicates explaination in domain_1: {'(rema_np__p_married ?p1 - entity ?p2 - entity)': "relation 'rema np  p married' holds; arguments: ?p1 is a entity, ?p2 is a entity; used as effect of king_proposes_marriage, precondition of princess_accepts_with_heart, effect of suitors_retire_due_to_phrase", '(with_all_my_heart_spoken)': "the state 'with all my heart spoken' holds; used as precondition of princess_accepts_with_heart, effect of princess_accepts_with_heart"}

domain_2:
    action in domain_2: (:action stepmother_orders_huntsman_to_kill_snow_white :parameters (?c ?h ?s - entity) :precondition (and (envious ?s) (snow__p_alive ?h) (snow__p_alive ?c)) :effect (fair ?s))
    predicates explaination in domain_2: {'(envious ?e - entity)': "entity ?e is in the state 'envious'; used as effect of stepmother_becomes_envious_of_snow_white, precondition of stepmother_orders_huntsman_to_kill_snow_white", '(fair ?e - entity)': "entity ?e is in the state 'fair'; used as effect of queen_wishes_child_white_red_black, effect of king_marries_stepmother, precondition of stepmother_becomes_envious_of_snow_white, effect of stepmother_orders_huntsman_to_kill_snow_white, effect of prince_marries_snow_white", '(snow__p_alive ?e - entity)': "entity ?e is in the state 'snow  p alive'; used as precondition of queen_pricks_finger, precondition of queen_wishes_child_white_red_black, precondition of child_is_born_and_queen_dies, effect of child_is_born_and_queen_dies, precondition of king_marries_stepmother, precondition of stepmother_asks_looking_glass_fairest, precondition of stepmother_becomes_envious_of_snow_white, precondition of stepmother_orders_huntsman_to_kill_snow_white"}

Please judge whether the two operators can be merged into one action based on following rules:
(1) If the two actions have the same name, they MUST be merged into one action;
(2) If the two actions are semantically equivalent (although they may differ in preconditions and effects), merge them. Genrally, you need to union their preconditions and effects.
(3) Note that do NOT merge two actions if the logic becomes more complex after merging. For example, do NOT use "or", "when" to union two actions (about their preconditions and effects). Namely NOT too general. 
(4) Do NOT invent any predicate.
(5) If you decide to merge two actions. You can invent new action name. But the new name must be reasonable according to the whole predicates in the action.
    For example: if the action expresses the meaning of "pick some object from drawer" according to the predicates in preconditions and effects, just name it like "pick_from_drawer", instead of "pick_from_container", etc.
(6) Keep the given PDDL style. Please use PDDL 1.0 and do NOT use Conditional Effects like "when", etc.
(7) Note the number of brackets in the PDDL format.

Your output should include four part:
(1) reasoning: your analysis process;
(2) merge_flag: whether the two operators can be merged into one;
(3) new_operator_name: if equivalent, output the new operator name (in one of the given operator or a new invented operator).
(4) new_operator: if equivalent, output the new operator in PDDL format.

If "merge_flag" is false, the "new_operator_name" and "new_operator" parts are null.

Your output should be in JSON format like below:
{
    "reasoning": "your analysis process",
    "merge_flag": true,
    "new_operator_name": "open_door",
    "new_operator": "(:action open_door \n :parameters (?r ?d) \n :precondition (and (hand_free ?r)) \n :effect (and (is_open ?d)))"
}

Do NOT output any strange symbols like "\".

The second action is `stepmother_orders_huntsman_to_kill_snow_white`, which requires the stepmother to be envious of snow white, and snow white to be alive. These two actions have completely different scenarios and predicates. They cannot be merged into one action. The predicates are also different, so they are not equivalent.
